title: Open Redirect in RedirectScheme Middleware via Absolute RequestURI Host Extraction
analysis:
The Traefik `RedirectScheme` middleware is vulnerable to an open redirect when an attacker sends a request with an absolute URI in the HTTP request line.

### Data Flow Path:
1. **Source**: An untrusted HTTP request is sent with an absolute URL in the request line, such as `GET http://evil.com/login HTTP/1.1`. Go's `net/http` parser populates `req.RequestURI` with this absolute URL.
2. **Data Propagation**: The request is routed to the `RedirectScheme` middleware. The `clientRequestURL` method in `pkg/middlewares/redirect/redirect_scheme.go` extracts the host and scheme from `req.RequestURI` using `uriRegexp`:
   ```go
   if match := uriRegexp.FindStringSubmatch(req.RequestURI); len(match) > 0 {
       scheme = match[1]
       if len(match[2]) > 0 {
           host = match[2] // Overwrites the host with "evil.com"
       }
       ...
   }
   ```
   This constructs an untrusted `oldURL` string `"http://evil.com/login"`.
3. **Sink**: The main `redirect` middleware uses `ReplaceAllString` on `oldURL` to build `newURL` (e.g., `"https://evil.com/login"`). If `newURL != oldURL`, it creates a `moveHandler` and writes the rewritten URL directly to the HTTP `Location` response header in `pkg/middlewares/redirect/redirect.go`:
   ```go
   rw.Header().Set("Location", m.location.String())
   ```

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To exploit this open redirect, an attacker can craft a raw HTTP request targeting the proxy's IP/port:
```http
GET http://attacker-controlled.com/malicious-page HTTP/1.1
Host: legitimate-target-site.com
Connection: close
```
Since the `RedirectScheme` middleware extracts and trusts the host from the request line, it will issue a `301/302` redirect to `https://attacker-controlled.com/malicious-page` instead of `https://legitimate-target-site.com/malicious-page`.
